Welcome to RecallDreams!

I’m a solo developer at RecallDreams, and I’m currently working on my second major project:

Echoes of the Threshold

A narrative puzzle game about exploring your own memories to escape a life-sized, ever-shifting maze. You wake up inside an immense, labyrinthine building that feels both deeply familiar and completely alien. Every corridor, every room, every staircase is a fragment of a memory, some comforting, some painful, some distorted. Nothing is quite right. The architecture bends and rearranges itself according to what you remember… and what you’ve tried to forget. Your only way out is to reassemble your own past.
By interacting with objects, reliving moments, solving symbolic puzzles, and choosing which memories to preserve or let fade, you slowly uncover the truth of how you ended up trapped here. Every path is a potential clue.
Every memory is both a key and a cage. “Echoes of the Threshold” is a slow, atmospheric, and deeply personal experience about memory, identity, and what it truly means to find your way home. Currently developed by one person.
One building.
One mind.

More to come soon.

Being a solo dev

Vision is clear, but dev time is limited.

My dev routine

7 days a week, in my spare time, I’ve been working on Echoes of the Threshold since early 2024, as a chilling project I started on my birthday.
Slowly, patiently, and with way too much tea.

› Buy me a tea

Daytime job

After completing my Licence in Philosophy, I became a university professor.

Teaching gave me a deep understanding of how the human mind works, something that now deeply influences my game development.

› Pantheon Sorbonne

Not really “solo”

Schrödinger, my black cat dev partner, supervises every line of code, tests the comfort of my keyboard, and reminds me that some memories are best contemplated with a warm presence nearby.

› Schrödinger's instagram

What if you were the game?

You don’t play Echoes of the Threshold.
You wake up inside it.

The core concept

“You don’t play the game. The game plays you.”

Every wall is built from your own memories. Every corridor shifts as you remember or forget.
A deeply personal experience that asks the question:

“What makes a memory worth keeping?”

› Discover more

Unique Gameplay

A philosophical puzzle game where your memory is both the tool and the puzzle.

  • Your way of remembering literally reshapes the level around you.
  • No traditional inventory, no map, no combat.
  • You must reassemble fragmented memories to change the architecture of the building.

Human & Authentic Touch

A deeply intimate game created by one person.

Made after long days at my daytime job, fuelled by endless cups of tea and the company of my cat Schrödinger.

No big studio. Just one man’s obsession with memory, identity, and what remains when everything else fades.
